Hey, I heard you're really good with knives. Can you show me some tips for making sure they stay sharp longer?
Keep the knife blade dry and use a honing steel regularly to maintain its edge.
Can you show me how to properly use a honing steel? I've never done it before and want to make sure I'm doing it right.
Hold the honing steel at a 20-degree angle against the blade, running the blade up the length of the steel several times on each side. This helps realign the cutting edge without sharpening it.
Got it, but how do I know if 20 degrees is right? And what if my knife still feels dull after doing that?

For the angle, imagine holding a pencil upright; the angle from the blade to the steel should be about as wide as your thumb at its widest point. If your knife still feels dull, it might need actual sharpening rather than just honing. Consider getting a professional sharpener every few months if needed.
